thread:
jordan: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: procurement / p-card / spend controls. a few concrete Qs: who signs off on infra purchases under $5k vs $5k-$50k, what's changed for p-card limits, and what's the expedited path for urgent vendor onboarding? cc @camille @rahul

camille (CFO): great questions — short answers up front then details. runway ~15 months at current burn; we're keeping a conservative spend posture. primary changes: clearer approval bands, stricter vendor onboarding SLA, and an emergency override flow. see below.

jordan: thanks — can you spell out the approval bands?

camille (CFO): yes. new bands effective immediately: < $3k: manager-level approval (no procurement ticket required); $3k–$25k: finance + procurement approval required; $25k–$250k: procurement + finance director sign-off; > $250k: CFO + legal + procurement, and vendor must complete enterprise onboarding. these replace the older thresholds.

jordan: noted. p-card limits?

camille (CFO): default p-card single-transaction cap stays at $3k. monthly rolling cap is $12k. exceptions possible for project leads via the Spend Request form (link below) and require 2 approvals. cards must not be used for vendor onboarding fees > $3k — those go through procurement and PO.

rahul (procurement): adding process notes: vendor onboarding SLA is now 7 business days for standard vendors (reference checks + security questionnaire), 15 business days for elevated-risk vendors. please file the onboarding packet in the portal; incomplete packets will pause approvals.

jess: for infra (cloud/GPU) bursts that are time sensitive, what's the expedited path?

camille (CFO): good one. we have an "expedite" path for infra emergencies: submit an urgent Spend Request, tag "expedite-infra", and ping @rahul + @lina. procurement will triage and can provision a temporary PO or approve a p-card exception for up to $10k while onboarding completes. CFO approval still required for > $25k but we aim to unblock within 48 hours for infra ops when justified.

lina (ops): to add, the ops team has a small contingency pool we can tap for sub-$15k urgent purchases without changing commitments — meant for burst fixes. coordinate with ops@redwood to use it.

nick (finance-bot): FYI: automated spend guardrail alerts will be enabled for any single user approaching 80% of monthly p-card cap. you'll see a DM and an email.

olivia (legal): note on contracts: any contract with indemnity, data residency, or SLA clauses that affect customer-facing services must go to legal even if under $25k. use the contract intake template when you submit.

jordan: thanks — can you paste the Spend Request link and a quick email subject template we should use when pinging procurement?

camille (CFO): sure — submit here: https://internal.redwood.com/spend-request (internal only). Email template: 

```
Subject: Spend Request — Project X — VendorName — Est $XXXX — Expedite: yes/no
Body: short summary, justification, cost center, requested approvers, attach onboarding packet if vendor
```

camille (CFO): i'll also post a short doc in #docs and update the procurement runbook this afternoon.

rahul (procurement): one operational note: if you're replacing an existing vendor, mark it as "replacement" in the form and attach the termination plan for the old vendor — that speeds review.

jess: how does this affect Dedicated capacity commitments (reserved capacity buys)? those tend to be > $250k sometimes.

camille (CFO): Reserved capacity is treated like an enterprise contract. Sales ops creates the initial term sheet, procurement and legal negotiate, and CFO signs for financials. anything with multiyear commit or > $250k needs explicit CFO approval and must include a run-rate impact assessment (impact on monthly burn and runway).

jordan: last one — any change to hiring/headcount approvals tied to this?

camille (CFO): hiring is on a scoped pause for non-critical roles. critical hire exceptions go through your VP + people ops + finance. we are prioritizing product/infra hires that directly reduce unit economics or unblock revenue.

jordan: super helpful, thanks. i'll distribute to my team.

rahul (procurement): i'll run a quick office hours tomorrow 11:00–11:30 for folks with pending requests or questions — drop into #calendar to register.

lina (ops): leaving this here: if you need the ops contingency fund, DM me with a 1–2 sentence justification and ETA for procurement completion.

nick (finance-bot): Audit trail note: this thread will be archived into the spend-controls channel doc set automatically.

jordan: appreciated everyone :thumbsup:
